review_candidates.title: Technical Operations Engineer, Systems & Fabric
review_candidates.description: Job Description IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe, and APAC. With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way: responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in. Cloud Operations & SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) runs the IREN AI Cloud the way a hyperscaler runs theirs. Every GPU-hour we sell is available, observable, supported and billed accurately. We are growing fast as new sites come online. We do it AI-native: the assistant drafts, and a named human verifies, signs and posts. We are seeking a Technical Operations Engineer to join our Level 2 Technical Operations team in Fort Worth or Sydney. The team keeps the GPU fleet healthy 24×7: compute nodes, firmware, Kubernetes, Slurm, InfiniBand fabric and storage. You take the incidents the L1 engineers cannot close, and you own them to root cause. This is a Level 2 role on our support ladder, and it is a destination. You diagnose in your lane, you run changes to a standard, and you write down what you found. A blank handoff is not a handoff here. The step above you is Senior Technical Operations Engineer. The SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) org is our L3; it owns SLOs (service level objectives), automation, and post-mortems. An escalation to it carries your diagnosis. We operate an AI-native operations function, and we are specific about what that means. The assistant drafts your ticket evidence and your handover card; you verify every line before it posts. A triage agent in Jira suggests the runbook and a classification. You confirm, correct or escalate every suggestion, and that logged response is a core KPI (key performance indicator). You use Claude Code under our engineering rules to turn a runbook into tested code. A named person is accountable for every output that leaves the building. The assistant drafts; a person verifies, signs and posts. We measure the work, never the tool. Job Requirements Two to five years operating or supporting HPC (high-performance computing) clusters in production or in an operations center or NOC (network operations center). Linux depth. You read logs, kernel messages and hardware events, and you know what they mean. Working knowledge of Kubernetes (bare metal a plus): triage workloads, read cluster state, run documented procedures. Operational experience with the Slurm workload manager: job triage, queue and node health, scheduler escalation. Hardware fundamentals: the BMC (baseboard management controller), iDRAC, Redfish and the SEL; the firmware and BIOS lifecycle on GPU servers. Working knowledge of the fabric and storage behind HPC: InfiniBand and Ethernet fabrics, UFM, and scale-out storage such as Weka or VAST Data. Observability tooling: Prometheus and Grafana, Splunk or Datadog; alert and log triage; runbook execution. Practical scripting (Python or Bash). You write and maintain automation, not only run it. Genuinely AI-native. You use AI assistants and agentic tools every day, not now and then. Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini is your daily driver, and Claude Code or an equivalent is how you build. You join systems up with Claude projects, the Atlassian and Microsoft 365 connectors, Jira Automation and Teams workflows. You can describe a workflow you automated, what broke and how you fixed it. For you, prompting is a way of working, not a party trick. Evidence before action, and that includes the assistant’s output. Every identifier in your update comes from a check you ran. A failed query reads “not found”; you never fill it in. You count from data, you never estimate, and you re-verify anything that looks too clean. Every ticket comment meets the same standard. It lists what you checked, what you found with source and time, what is not verified, and who acts next. Clear written and spoken communication: incident updates, handover notes, runbook and RCA (root cause analysis) text the next region can act on. Comfortable on a 12-hour rotating roster in a 24×7 operations center, with a structured written handover into and out of the adjacent region. Post-secondary education in computer science or engineering is an asset; equivalent hands-on experience counts the same. This role works 12-hour rotating shifts in a 24×7 operations center: 4 days on / 3 days off, then 3 days on / 4 days off. On-call participation and major incident response are part of the role. The role is office-based with periodic site visits; you travel to project locations in the US, Canada or Australia as required. Pre-employment screening, including background check and, where applicable, substance testing, may be required according to company policies. Nice to have CKA or CKAD (the Kubernetes administrator or developer certification), Linux+ or RHCSA (Red Hat Certified System Administrator). ITIL (the IT service management framework) Foundation, CompTIA Server+, or NVIDIA data center certifications. Working understanding of a public cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) and how it integrates with on-premises HPC. GPU fault vocabulary: XID (the NVIDIA driver fault code) errors, NVSwitch and NVLink, and DCGM (NVIDIA’s data center GPU manager) diagnostics. You have built a small tool, dashboard or bot because it was faster than asking. Experience in a fast-growth environment where the fleet doubled and the process had to hold. What will make you unhappy here You want to dispatch hands before you have read the log. You would rather work the same node ticket again than write the tool that retires it. You want a stable, predictable week. “The AI wrote it” is, to you, a defense rather than an admission. What success looks like (first 12 months) Your tickets stay inside the Level 2 team: routing to hands excluded, the team target is over 80% kept within 12 months. Firmware and provisioning work stays inside the Level 2 team: the team target is over 85%. Every handoff and handover you post carries an evidence comment; the monthly audit shows 95%. First substantive comment within two hours on every ticket you own, at the 90th percentile. Four merged automations in IREN GitLab with tests by month 12, one of them in use by another engineer. Four problem records raised on repeat patterns, with the fixes SRE designed executed by you and no recurrence. Every escalation you send to SRE arrives with the diagnosis; none comes back as L2 work with a runbook attached. Job Responsibilities Level 2 incident ownership in the Systems and Fabric lane Take the systems incident the runbook cannot close, and own it to root cause. Provide Level 2 operational support for the HPC (high-performance computing) cloud environment within SLA (service level agreement) targets. Monitor, troubleshoot and resolve complex incidents across Kubernetes, Slurm, cluster management, fabric and storage. Read the SEL and the Redfish state as the first comment on every node ticket, before any hands dispatch. Post the first substantive comment within two hours of acknowledgment on every ticket you own. Hand off and hand over only with an evidence comment attached; an escalation to SRE carries your diagnosis. Supply the ticket evidence for the post mortem SRE writes after a Sev 1 or Sev 2, within one business day of the bridge. Take part in the on-call rotation and in major incident bridges as the systems lead. Change, firmware and operational readiness Run firmware, provisioning and changes to a standard, every time. Execute patches, firmware updates, upgrades and maintenance under the change management process, with a tested rollback. Run firmware, BIOS and BMC (baseboard management controller) reflashes from the runbook, and record the verifiable execution evidence. Support tooling integration and operational readiness for new HPC capability before handover into production support. Operate and maintain monitoring, alerting and observability tooling; tune one noisy alert per quarter. Automation, runbooks and the record Retire the repeat ticket instead of working it again. Contribute one merged, reviewed automation per quarter in IREN GitLab, with tests: node-state triage, the firmware runbook as code, a UFM baseline-and-diff, event bursts. Keep ticket fields (category, vendor, component) accurate so we can measure the fleet. AI-native practice Use the assistant for every draft, and verify every identifier before it posts. Confirm, correct or escalate every triage-agent suggestion in Jira; the logged response rate on eligible tickets is a core KPI, target 80%. Verify every identifier in an assistant-drafted update against a check you ran; report a failed query as “not found”. Build with Claude Code under our engineering rules: code in IREN GitLab, tests before merge, secret scanning on, no credentials in prompts. Name what the assistant got wrong in the monthly lab, and feed the correction back. Mentoring and coverage Lift L1, and keep eyes on glass. Give technical guidance to the L1 engineers and DC (data center) technicians; take one shadow shift per quarter with an L1 engineer. Deliver the shift handover as a written card: open incidents, pending changes and watch items.
